section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through performing mitzvos, the vessels of Zeir Anpin are built and light is drawn into them, and this principle applies to all levels of the spiritual chain, including the shofar, tefillin, emotions, and speech.
section.t: And it is explained in the maamar
(beginning with the words "Adon Olam"13),
that through the performance of the mitzvos, the construction of the vessels of Zeir Anpin is accomplished,
and also the drawing down of the light into the vessels of Zeir Anpin.
And this matter also applies to
(the beginning of the continuation)
the festival of Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat, in the Temple they would sound [the shofar] but not in the rest of the country14,
as it is explained in the maamar of the Admo"r HaTzemach Tzedek15
(upon which the maamar said on Erev Rosh HaShanah is based)
the reason why on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat they do not sound [the shofar] in the rest of the country,
because our mitzvos are
(in order)
that through an arousal from below there is an arousal from above,
that through the performance of the mitzvos by man, the supernal mitzvos are made
(the 248 commandments are the 248 limbs of the King16).
For similarly, it is also with the mitzvah of sounding the shofar, whose purpose is to thereby make the aspect of the supernal shofar,
and therefore on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat they do not sound [the shofar]
(in the rest of the country),
because on Shabbat there is the aspect of the supernal shofar
(the aspect of delight)
even without the work of man,
by virtue of Shabbat,
and Shabbat is inherently sanctified and established17.
And that in the Temple they would sound [the shofar] even on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat is because in the Temple,
which is the gate of heaven18,
there was the ability to make a more elevated aspect in delight
(as is explained at length in the maamar of Erev Rosh HaShanah).
And this matter,
that the supernal mitzvos
(the matters)
are made specifically through the performance of the mitzvos by man,
applies to all the levels and all the partzufim of the entire order of the chain of descent,
according to the teaching of the Rav HaMaggid19
in his explanation of the Mishnah20
"Know what is above you" — that everything that is above is from you.
For the aspect of delight
(shofar)
that is above is made
(as above)
through the performance of the mitzvah of sounding the shofar,
and the aspect of the supernal intellects
(which are the matter of tefillin,
as is known21
that the four portions are the aspect of the four intellects)
is made through the performance of the mitzvah of tefillin,
for through man laying tefillin, he causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to lay tefillin22,
and so too with the emotions
(of Zeir Anpin),
for through the man below performing the mitzvah of "And you shall love the Lord your God" and the mitzvah of "The Lord your God you shall fear"23
(for love and fear are the root of all the mitzvos24)
thereby the construction of Zeir Anpin is made,
and so too with the aspect of Malchus,
for the construction of the world of speech
(Malchus)
is made through the speech of the lower man in words of Torah and words of prayer.
And this is the content of the matter of the performance of the mitzvos
(according to what is explained in these maamarim),
for the supernal levels are
(generally)
in the number 248
(the 248 limbs of the King),
and the construction of all the supernal levels is through the performance of the 248 positive commandments
(of man),
and as it is written25
"And you shall do them,"
"you" is written,
"I consider it as if you have made Me"26.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between two levels of fulfilling mitzvos: one for the sake of achieving the purpose of the command, and a higher level where the act itself creates a new, transcendent will, rooted in the essence of the Jewish soul.
section.t: And it needs to be understood,
behold it is known27
that the superiority in the performance of mitzvos is when the performance is because this is the command of the Holy One, blessed be He
(and as per the wording of the blessing over mitzvos, "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us")
and not because of the reason28
and the virtue inherent in them,
including also the reason that through the performance of the mitzvos, the supernal mitzvos are made.
And the explanation of this can be said as follows,
that in the mitzvos
(the will and command from above that the children of Israel should perform the mitzvos)
there are two matters.
The cause and reason for the command,
and from this comes into being the reality of the mitzvah
(the command),
which is an effect of the reason.
And afterwards
(after the supernal command)
comes the performance of the mitzvah by the man who fulfills them.
And in this there are two general modes.
The first mode is that he fulfills it for the purpose of the command
(so that the reason of the command will be completed),
and the second mode is that he fulfills it in a more elevated manner,
that his performance of the mitzvah is in a way that through it he makes, as it were, a new will,
which is incomparably higher than the will that is the effect of the reason.
For since Israel are rooted in the Essence
(the Master of the Will),
"Israel and the King are alone together"29,
therefore when Israel performs a mitzvah,
he has the ability to make a new will that did not exist before this.
And it can be said that corresponding to this are the two interpretations of the statement of our sages, of blessed memory30,
"A pleasing satisfaction before Me that I spoke and My will was done"31.
The first interpretation is,
that through the performance of the mitzvah, the will
(the command)
that existed initially is fulfilled.
And the second interpretation of "My will was done" is,
that through the performance of the mitzvah by Israel
(as in the second mode)
there is made
(there is innovated)
a new will that did not exist before this
(in the manner explained in many places32
regarding the interpretation of "they do the will of the Omnipresent"33,
that the meaning of "they do" is that they make a new will).
And based on this, it can be said,
that what is stated in the above discourses, that the purpose of the mitzvos is in order to thereby make the supernal mitzvos,
this is in the first mode of the performance of the mitzvos,
in the aspect of fulfilling the will that is the effect of the reason,
so that there will be the construction of the entire order of the chain of descent,
the 248 limbs of the King
[And in this itself there are two matters,
one,
the reason and cause
(of the will)
– that the mitzvos
(the levels)
should come into being above.
Two,
the effect – the will that Israel should perform the mitzvos below].
But the performance of mitzvos from the aspect that Israel are rooted in the Essence is to make a new will.
And this is what is explained in many discourses27
that the superiority in the performance of mitzvos is when the performance is because this is the will
(command)
of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and not because of the reason
(including also the reason that through the performance of the mitzvos the supernal mitzvos are made),
for this will is a will that is above reason.
And the performance of the mitzvos
(from the aspect of this will)
is not in order to effect matters above,
but rather,
"mitzvah" from the term "tzavta" and connection34,
the unification of Israel with the Master of the Will,
and even to the unification with the Essence.
And in the manner of the statement of the Alter Rebbe35
"I want nothing at all — I do not want your Gan Eden, I do not want your World to Come, etc. — I want nothing more than You alone."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section resolves an apparent contradiction by explaining that the particular delight in each mitzvah relates to the will that is an effect of the reason, while the general will in all mitzvos equally is higher, relating to the new will that Israel creates.
section.t: And based on this, it will also be understood what is explained in the above discourse of the Admo"r HaTzemach Tzedek36,
that the particular delight in each mitzvah,
that in each mitzvah there is a unique delight,
is more elevated than the general delight and will that is common to all the mitzvos equally,
and its root is from the aspect of the source of delights
(which is above the aspect of the revelation of delight),
for at first glance it is not understood how this aligns with what is explained in many discourses27
that the general intention that is common to all the mitzvos equally
("and He commanded us")
is more elevated than the particular intention of each individual mitzvah.
And the explanation of this can be said as follows,
that in the above discourse of the Admo"r HaTzemach Tzedek, it speaks about the matter of the will in the mitzvos as it is an effect of the reason,
in order that the supernal mitzvos should come into being.
And what is explained there, that in the mitzvos there are two levels,
the general matter that is common to all the mitzvos equally,
and the particular matter of each individual mitzvah,
behold these two levels are within the will that comes from the reason.
For at the beginning of its flow it is a general will that the matters above should be made through the performance of the mitzvos by man,
and from this there subsequently flows
(to a lower level)
a particular will for each and every individual mitzvah,
in order that through its performance, that particular supernal mitzvah which corresponds to it should be made
(through the shofar below,
the shofar above.
And similarly with the rest of the mitzvos).
And therefore it says there that there is an advantage in the particular delight and intention
(and even that the root of the particular delight specifically is in the aspect of the source of delights),
because the intention in this will is to make the supernal mitzvos
(particular matters)
above,
and this is accomplished specifically through the particular action of each mitzvah.
And what is explained in many discourses, that the general intention that is common to all the mitzvos equally is more elevated,
is,
because there it speaks about the will that Israel innovates and makes through their service,
and from the aspect of this will,
the mode of the performance of the mitzvos is to do [His] will,
a general intention.
